title: To know one another
hookLine: God made nations and tribes that you may know one another (Quran 49:13)
tomorrow: can anyone be made to believe? the Quran answers in one line.

lines: THE TOAST TURNS TO THE ROOM.
cards: Halfway through a wedding toast, the speaker turns from the couple to the whole room, and everyone sits up. Surah 49 of the Quran has a turn like that. Verse after verse speaks to believers: "O ye who believe!"
Don't let one people mock another. Shun much suspicion. Don't spy, don't backbite.
Then verse thirteen changes who's listening: "O mankind!" Why the switch? That was yesterday's question.

teach.b: Because this verse is for everyone.

In Pickthall's words: "O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another. Lo! the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct."
The differences are made on purpose, and the purpose is knowing, not ranking. Not birth, not tribe: the verse measures nobility by conduct. A story puts a face on it.
Tradition says that when Mecca opened to the Prophet, the man chosen to climb onto the Kaaba and call the prayer was Bilal, a freed slave of Abyssinian descent.
Some commentators say a few onlookers sneered at him that day, and link this verse to it.

Whether or not that's its occasion, the Prophet's farewell sermon, as reported in the Musnad of Ahmad, says the same thing plainly: no Arab over a non-Arab, no non-Arab over an Arab, and no color over another, except by righteousness.
So, in this verse, peoples and tribes are made for knowing one another, not for ranking. In that telling, the voice calling the prayer from the Kaaba that day belonged to a freed slave.

how: Muslim preachers and teachers cite Quran 49:13 and the farewell sermon together when they speak about race, tribe and the equal dignity of believers.

games.q: what does “to know one another” mean?
o: made different to show which people is best
made different so each people keeps to itself
made different so people would learn each other

games.q: Quran 49:13, piece by piece: tap the pairs.
p: that ye may know one another
called the prayer from the Kaaba

s: Quran 49:13 is addressed only to Muslims
it switches from 'O ye who believe' to 'O mankind'.
in 49:13, the noblest is the one best in conduct
not the best-born; the verse names conduct alone.
the verse treats differences between peoples as a mistake to erase
God made the nations and tribes, it says, so people would know one another.

games.q: a friend says 49:13 proves background doesn't matter, so nobody should ever ask where anyone's from. what does the verse itself add?
o: the differences are made on purpose, so we can know one another.
she's right: the verse wants every people to look and live the same.
the verse ranks the tribes, so it's polite never to bring them up.
games.why: rank comes only from conduct, but the nations and tribes have a purpose: 'that ye may know one another.'

practice: On a scrap of paper, write the name of one person you see often but don't really know. Under it, write one question about where they come from that you'd honestly like answered: a place, a dish, a word their grandmother used.
